description: An attending physician must decide whether to authorize a medically stable patient's enrollment in the hospital-at-home program and finalize the operational safeguards for the first day, with input from hospital-at-home nursing, pharmacy, social work, and utilization review.

shared_context.S1: The patient is medically stable and is being considered for enrollment in the hospital-at-home program tomorrow.
shared_context.S2: The patient has said that returning home would be preferable if the care plan can be safely arranged.
shared_context.S3: The hospital-at-home program can provide in-home clinical visits, medication delivery, remote monitoring, and scheduled video follow-up.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Shah signs the final enrollment order and care plan.
shared_context.S5: The program's standing pre-enrollment huddle reviews nursing, pharmacy, home-support, and coverage requirements before Dr. Shah signs the order.

PF1.text: Lena's first-day nursing assessment requires exactly two in-home skilled-nursing visits, with the first visit at 08:00, because the patient needs an early assessment and an evening reassessment; those visit requirements are in the nursing intake worksheet but not yet in the enrollment order.

PF2.text: Victor confirmed that the discharge medication must be transported refrigerated and delivered to the home by exactly 07:30 tomorrow; the program pharmacy has accepted this delivery arrangement, but it is not yet recorded in the care plan.

PF3.text: Naomi confirmed that the patient's caregiver can provide in-home support only from 10:00 through 18:00 tomorrow and has agreed to be present during that interval; the availability was confirmed by phone but is not documented in the social-work note.

PF4.text: Eli verified that the insurer's authorization permits hospital-at-home enrollment only if a video clinician check is scheduled within 24 hours of arrival home; utilization review has the approval reference, but the condition is not yet attached to the enrollment order.

acceptance_conditions: The patient must be enrolled in hospital-at-home.
The first day must include exactly two skilled-nursing visits, with the first at 08:00.
The medication must be delivered refrigerated by 07:30 tomorrow.
The caregiver support window must be recorded as 10:00-18:00 tomorrow.
A video clinician check must be scheduled within 24 hours of arrival home.
A refrigerated medication-delivery commitment must be documented.
The 08:00 nursing visit must be documented as a care-plan commitment.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'medication_delivery' and c['target'] == 'Patient home' and c['detail'] == 'refrigerated delivery by 07:30 tomorrow' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'nursing_visit' and c['target'] == 'Patient home' and c['detail'] == 'first visit at 08:00' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The nursing worksheet changes the first-day schedule from an unspecified visit plan to exactly two visits and fixes the first visit at 08:00, which also enables the required nursing-visit commitment.
The pharmacy confirmation changes medication logistics from an unspecified delivery to refrigerated delivery at exactly 07:30 tomorrow and requires the matching documented commitment.
The caregiver confirmation changes the support plan from an unspecified availability to the exact 10:00-18:00 tomorrow window.
The insurer condition changes the coverage plan from an unspecified follow-up to a required video clinician check scheduled within 24 hours of arrival home.
